what_it_does: An analog-to-digital converter (ADC) is a chip that converts continuous analog signals into digital numbers. This paper describes an ADC running at 10 billion samples per second with two parallel channels. The challenge is that at this speed, a single amplifier becomes a bottleneck. The design overlaps the residue transfer and quantization steps to eliminate this bottleneck and adds automatic power-gating to reduce unnecessary power consumption.
